title: Free expired leases without taking a renewed one

blocks.text: The build farm hands out time-limited leases on shared machines: build agents, GPUs, a plotter. A holder renews its lease before it runs out and releases it when done, and a sweeper thread frees the leases nobody renewed and tells their holders. Two incidents last month: a training job lost its GPU a few milliseconds after renewing it, and a CAD team that had released the plotter got a "your lease expired" message for it anyway.

`LeaseTable` already acquires, renews and releases. Write `sweep(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/LeaseTable.java`: free every lease that ran out at or before `now`, tell its holder, and return the resources it freed.
When you're done, a lease renewed while the sweep runs stays with its holder, and only leases the sweep itself freed are reported and returned. About six lines in total.
The tests force the interleaving: they make a holder renew or release its lease just before the sweeper changes that lease in the table, the way it happens when the holder's thread gets there first.

cases.says: a sweep frees every lease that ran out, tells each of their holders, returns their resources, and keeps the leases still running
a sweep before any lease ran out frees nothing and tells nobody
a lease its holder renews between the sweeper's check and its removal stays with the holder, with the new expiry
a lease its holder releases between the sweeper's check and its removal is neither returned as freed nor reported to the holder

origin.section: A Walk Hands Out Entries Read Earlier, So Act on One with remove(key, value)

concepts: A walk hands out entries read earlier, even ones removed since, so acting on one with remove(key) can remove a newer value; remove(key, value) removes only if the key still maps to the value checked.
